name: Dwarven Outfitters
summary: In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm offers new recruits a bargain. Hunt wolves for their tough meat, and he provides sturdy gloves against Dun Morogh's cold.

sections.title: A Fair Trade in Coldridge
sections.body: Cold reaches every path through Coldridge Valley. Outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm asks new recruits to hunt wolves in the snowy drifts and bring their tough meat to the outpost. In return, he gives them gloves to guard their hands from the cold.

sections.title: Living Off the Valley
sections.body: Wolves threaten the dwarven scouts and young gnomes training in the valley. Yet they also feed the garrison at Anvilmar. Hunting them makes the paths between local encampments somewhat safer. Stoutarm's bargain tests recruits against local wildlife and adds food for the bitter nights ahead.

faq.answer: Sten Stoutarm is a dwarf stationed outside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. He looks after newly arrived recruits and offers practical gear in return for hunting local game.

faq.q: Why does Sten need wolf meat?
faq.answer: Anvilmar's outpost relies on local hunting to keep its supplies stocked. Wolf meat feeds the troops and trainers who live in the secluded, snowbound valley.

faq.q: Where do you find the wolves for this task?
faq.answer: Wolves roam the snowy clearings throughout Coldridge Valley, especially beyond Anvilmar's main courtyard and along the paths to the outlying camps.
Sten gives recruits a pair of warm gloves to guard their hands from Dun Morogh's bitter winds.

faq.q: Is wolf meat considered good food among dwarves?
faq.answer: Wolf meat is tough, coarse, and chewy, but dwarves in Dun Morogh's harsh mountain climate prize hearty, filling food over fine dining. Stewed or roasted over a campfire, it feeds the garrison.

faq.q: Can gnomes do this quest too?
faq.answer: Yes. Gnomes training alongside their dwarven allies in Coldridge Valley face the same biting winds and need warm clothing.

angles.text: As a young Bronzebeard dwarf in Coldridge Valley, you learn to provide for the camp and respect the mountain cold.
As a gnome taking refuge with your dwarven cousins in Dun Morogh, you need practical mountain clothing to endure the cold at Anvilmar, along with a sharp mind.
